title: Spinner Wheel Chess | Can I Beat Martin?
summary: Spinner Wheel Chess episode 1 vs Martin (250): before each of his moves the creator spins a wheel with segments Move / Capture / Check / Blunder that dictates what kind of move he must make. He plays passively (e3, Nf3, Be2, O-O) to limit forced options, but the wheel keeps demanding checks and blunders (he loses a bishop to a forced 'blunder' Be3), Martin plays surprisingly principled chess, and Martin forces a mating net on h6/g4 - he loses episode 1.
rules: Normal chess vs Martin (250), standard start.

Spin the wheel before each of your moves. Segments: MOVE - play any move you like; CAPTURE - you must make a legal capture even if it loses material; CHECK - you must give a legal check even if it blunders; BLUNDER - you must actively try to lose at least 3 points of material.
If the required move type is impossible on the board (no legal capture/check/blunder), you play your best normal move instead.
If you are in check you must still get out of check (the wheel result must be compatible with legality).
Bot (Martin) moves normally without a wheel.
win_condition: Checkmate Martin despite the wheel; episode 1 result: loss.
